# A Topic is generated by a model, then verified against a real search

Stage 2 must show the student 5 to 8 Topics inside the Domain they picked. Fynd asks a model for the Topics, and then searches Semantic Scholar for the Topic the student picked. Fynd keeps the Topic only if the search returns 3 or more Papers with an open copy. A Topic that fails the check goes back to the student with the count shown.

Fynd stores no corpus of its own. Semantic Scholar is the index, and a Topic is a label for a search and not a Claim, so a Topic does not need the citation guard that protects the handover.

## Consequences

The contract is the part that must not change: a Topic reaches the student only if a real search returns enough open Papers for it. The generator behind that contract can change later. A grounded generator, which runs one broad search for the Domain, clusters the titles it gets back, and names each cluster, fits behind the same contract with no change downstream.

A Topic carries two fields. A label the student reads, and a query Fynd searches with. The model returns both in the same structured output, so no later Stage rewrites a label into a query.

The threshold of 3 counts Papers with an open copy, not raw search hits. The PRD allows open abstracts and open full text only, so a paywalled Paper never reaches stage 5. The threshold is one named constant.

The threshold moved from 5 to 3 on 2026-10-07, ahead of the Gap evidence this entry asked for. Two facts made the move safe. The Gap bar needs 3 Claims from independent Sources with at least one Paper and at least one Statistic or Product, so the Papers never had to carry all three. The Seeded Topic also returns 12 open Papers out of 20, so neither number binds there. The risk the lower number adds is a Topic that passes with exactly 3 Papers and then loses two to bad text extraction, so stage 4 carries a guard for that case. See the PRD.

A Topic under the threshold does not spend the student's Re-roll. The count shows next to that Topic and the rest of the list stays pickable, because a low count is information the student did not have and not a wasted turn. The Re-roll stays for the case where the whole list holds nothing they want.

The tried Topics and their counts live in the `stage_run` row while stage 2 is still running, because the student sees them again after a reload and the free container restarts. See the database design.

The round 2 prompt names the ten Topics to avoid, so a Re-roll asks the model a different question and the cache serves no stale list. See [ADR 0004](./0004-replayable-runs-and-versioned-prompts.md).

A Topic is a value on one Project and not a row in a shared table. Two model runs word the same Topic two different ways, so a shared table would need matching logic that buys nothing. The disk cache covers the repeated fetch cost instead.

## Considered options

A curated Topic list for each Domain. Rejected because a closed list needs a human to grow it, and the PRD already asks the model for 5 to 8 Topics.

A corpus Fynd owns, built by reading the papers in a Domain and storing them. Rejected because it is a data engineering project with no payoff, and a search API already holds that index.

A model with no verification. Rejected because the student only finds out at stage 4 that the Topic has no literature, and that is the failure Stage 2 exists to catch.

A count check on all 5 to 8 proposed Topics, before the student picks. Rejected because Semantic Scholar allows 1 request per second, so eight calls make a dropdown slow, and seven of the counts are thrown away.
